subject: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags

Team — kicking off a focused readout for our Nov KPI pack ahead of next week's QBR. Attached is a one-pager summary plus a short spreadsheet with per-model deltas. Please review and reply with any corrections/blocks by EOD so I can fold changes into the QBR deck. High level asks: 

1) Confirm any customer-impacting incidents (uptime < 99.95%) since Oct 25 and owner + ETA for mitigation.
2) Validate latency regressions called out on page 2 (p95 increase for streaming endpoints).
3) Call out any cost anomalies tied to Dedicated burst or cold-start inefficiencies.
4) Provide updated OKR progress % (only items touching latency/cost/throughput).

Attachments: 2026-11-dashboard-summary.pdf (pdf), prefix-cache-analysis.xlsx (xlsx)
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Prep-2026-KPI

Thanks — david
--
David Kim
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags

David — quick pass from Performance/Serving:

- Uptime: We had a brief regional controller fail in us-west-2 on 2026-11-02 at 03:38 UTC that caused ~38 minutes of elevated error rates for non-cached inference paths. Impact: customer-facing errors spiked to 0.6% for that window; overall monthly uptime stays at 99.96% after the incident credit/fix. Owner: infra-ops (Mitzi) — root cause was a rolling restart race; permanent fix scheduled 11/24.

- Latency: p50 stable (11 ms for short-text gen), p95 for streaming endpoints moved from 420ms -> 640ms over the month for models with sequence length > 1024. Preliminary cause: increased cold-cache misses after recent autoscaler tuning; prefix-cache hit rate dropped from 72% -> 58%. See prefix-cache-analysis.xlsx (sheet: hit-rate-by-model).

- Cost: overall token unit cost up ~8% month-over-month; primary driver is increased on-demand Dedicated bursts during peak (Sat-Thu evenings) — estimated $12k incremental on monthly run-rate. Working with finance to split committed vs burst attribution.

Action items:
- Marissa to publish a short remediation plan for prefix caching (prefetching & hot-list) by 11/23.
- Rishi to validate autoscaler rollback test and provide go/no-go for canary by 11/25.

Flagging: If we can’t recover p95 before QBR, recommend a one-slide callout and risk mitigation paragraph.

-Marissa
Senior Director, Serving Runtime

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags

Thanks — quick clarification on the autoscaler data and proposed rollback test plan: 

- Autoscaler change on 2026-10-28 increased max burst window from 10->18 nodes to reduce 429s at peak. That reduced 429s but increased cold-start frequency when instances cycled; cold-start penalty ~150-250ms on p95 for streaming.

- Proposed test: run a two-day controlled canary in eu-west-1 with old autoscaler params, synthetic traffic at 70/90/110% of baseline, measure p95 and cold-start rate. If p95 improves by >120ms without increased 429 rates, proceed with staged rollback. Timeline: test start 11/23; results by 11/25. Owner: rishi (infra experiments).

One more data point: we've instrumented a new metric "prefix_cache_miss_cost" to estimate token-level cost waste due to misses. Preliminary numbers: $0.9k/week in incremental decode compute. Will surface in the spreadsheet tomorrow.

-Rishi
VP, Infrastructure & Reliability

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags

Looping in OKR progress:

- OKR: Reduce production p95 latency for streaming by 25% (Q4 target). Current progress: 47% complete toward the target (calculated from baseline & partial rollout gains).
- OKR: Reduce inference unit cost by 15% via batching/quantization — Current: 62% complete; quantization experiments on smaller models rolled to prod (savings ~6% so far).
- Blocker: prefix-cache work is on the critical path to deliver the remaining latency gains. Marissa's remediation plan is therefore the gating item.

Please include a single slide mapping these two OKRs to the remediation milestones and the canary timeline — that will make the QBR ask clearer for execs.

-Soojin
Director, Product (Operations)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags

Thanks — Finance/Rev ops note:

- The $12k incremental Dedicated burst cost is real but partly offset by higher metered usage (customer growth in advertising vertical). Net margin impact estimated at ~$6k this month.
- If we need to call out a potential negative variance at QBR, recommend we also show the growth-linked revenue lift to avoid alarmism.
- Requested: Marissa/Rishi, please add the burst attribution numbers (committed vs burst) into the sheet by 11/23 so I can reconcile for QBR.

- Also: procurement has signaled longer lead times for additional Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 (8-10 weeks); if QBR decisions unlock committed capacity, we should list timeline tradeoffs.

- Grace
Head of Finance & RevOps

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Leadership Team <leadership@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Leadership KPI deep-check & QBR prep: November dashboard + flags

Great thread — pulling this into the QBR deck. TL;DR & next steps for slide bullets: 

- Incident: us-west-2 controller restart — root cause fix scheduled 11/24; impact limited, monthly uptime 99.96%. (Owner: Mitzi)
- Latency: p95 spike driven by prefix-cache miss rate + autoscaler burst churn; remediation plan + canary (11/23-11/25). (Owners: Marissa, Rishi)
- Cost: +8% token unit cost month-over-month; Dedicated burst ~$12k incremental; net margin hit ~6k. Finance to reconcile with growth lift. (Owner: Grace)
- OKR status: latency OKR 47% -> show path to 100% via prefix-cache + canary results; cost OKR 62% -> show remaining experiments and runway. (Owner: Soojin)

Action checklist for QBR slideset (I will assemble):
- Marissa: remediation plan text + expected p95 improvement (by 11/23).
- Rishi: canary results and instrumentation numbers for prefix_cache_miss_cost (by 11/25).
- Grace: burst attribution and margin reconciliation slide (by 11/24).
- Soojin: OKR progress bullet + final percent numbers (by 11/23).

If you prefer a 30-min dry-run with execs on Monday morning, shout here — I'm scheduling both Mon 09:00 and Mon 11:30 PT slots; will lock one if no objections by EOD today.

Thanks all — david
--
David Kim
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
